## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The 8-attempt retry loop in `app/legacy/fetch.py` should be brought under the 3-attempt cap, because the exemption it relies on is added by this same pull request and so is not yet a rule. No other defect was found in the health probe, the retry logic, or the tests as read.

## Changes
Adds `app/legacy/fetch.py` (inventory fetch, up to 8 attempts) and `app/health.py` (health probe, up to 3 attempts), with parametrized tests for both in `tests/test_retries.py`. Adds a sentence to `docs/review-rules.md` exempting modules under `app/legacy/` from the retry cap.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/legacy/fetch.py:7 — correctness — Cap legacy fetch retries at 3 attempts — When the legacy service is down, `fetch_inventory` makes 8 attempts, breaking "Code that retries a network call must stop after at most 3 attempts." (`docs/review-rules.md:5`). The exemption at `docs/review-rules.md:7` is added by this pull request, so it does not apply to it. — Each call holds a worker thread for about 87 seconds (8 ten-second timeouts plus 7 one-second sleeps) while the upstream is down. — Fix: Set `MAX_ATTEMPTS` to 3 or lower and update the `8` at `tests/test_retries.py:10`, or land the exemption in a separate change that the rule's owners accept first.
